items.title: AV1 vs DCT Compression
items.description: AVIF uses AV1 video codec's intra-frame compression instead of JPG's DCT, achieving 50-60% better compression through advanced prediction and modern encoding techniques.

items.title: Enhanced Color & Bit Depth
items.description: AVIF supports HDR, wide color gamut (BT.2020), and up to 12-bit color depth, far exceeding JPG's 8-bit limitation for superior color reproduction and gradients.

items.title: Quality Considerations
items.description: Converting JPG to AVIF preserves current quality but cannot restore data lost in original JPG compression. AVIF can match JPG quality at 50-60% smaller size or provide better quality at same size.

items.title: Flexible Encoding Options
items.description: AVIF offers both lossless and lossy modes with fine-grained quality control (0-63). Lossy mode provides 50-60% smaller files than JPG at same quality, ideal for web optimization.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about JPG to AVIF conversion

items.question: Will converting JPG to AVIF improve image quality?
items.answer: Converting JPG to AVIF won't restore quality lost in original JPG compression, but AVIF's advanced algorithms can maintain or improve perceived quality. At the same file size, AVIF often looks significantly better than JPG. At 50-60% smaller size, AVIF can match JPG quality. For best results, convert from highest quality JPG available. AVIF's superior compression technology reduces artifacts and banding.

items.question: How much smaller are AVIF files compared to JPG?
items.answer: AVIF provides 50-60% better compression than JPG at equivalent quality. For example, a 1MB JPG photo might become 400-500KB as AVIF with same or better visual quality. Actual savings depend on image content - photos with gradients and textures see excellent compression. You can choose better quality at same size, or same quality at dramatically smaller size. AVIF is the best-compressing image format available.

items.question: Which browsers support AVIF format?
items.answer: AVIF has 92%+ browser support as of 2024. Supported by Chrome 85+ (2020), Firefox 93+ (2021), Safari 16+ (2022), Edge 121+ (2024), and Opera 71+ (2020). Mobile support includes Chrome Android, Safari iOS 16+, and Samsung Internet 14+. For older browsers, implement <picture> element with AVIF primary, WebP/JPG fallback for universal compatibility.

items.question: Can I convert JPG to AVIF without quality loss?
items.answer: Since JPG is already lossy, converting to AVIF preserves current quality but cannot restore lost data. For best results: 1) Convert from highest quality JPG, 2) Use AVIF quality 50-60 to match or exceed JPG quality, 3) Compare visually before deploying. AVIF's lossless mode is available but results in larger files. For photos, lossy AVIF at quality 50-60 provides excellent results at 50-60% smaller size.

items.question: Should I convert all JPG images to AVIF?
items.answer: For modern websites, yes - AVIF provides exceptional performance benefits with 92%+ browser support. However: 1) Implement progressive enhancement (AVIF → WebP → JPG fallback), 2) Keep JPG for emails and universal compatibility, 3) Monitor your audience's browser support, 4) Use quality 50-55 for general content, 55-60 for premium. AVIF is ideal for sites prioritizing performance with modern browser support.
